description: The robot first raises its hand to head level, makes a small preparatory shift for emphasis, and then performs two sharp wrist flicks to simulate air quotes.
reasoning:

# Q2: candidates=P1) up+horizontal+x50,y65,z70, P2) front+vertical+x60,y60,z70; winner=P1 because its head-side placement and upward-pointing, horizontal-gripper geometry is the most iconic and readable pose for air quotes.
# Q3: options=M1 pose>movement(flick)>movement(flick), M2 pose(low)>pose(high)>movement(prep)>movement(flick); winner=M2 because staging the gesture by first raising the hand into the proper lane makes the subsequent sharp quotes much clearer.
# Q4: options=C1 small preparatory shoulder shift before the flicks, C2 a hold after the flicks, C3 a slow drift away after the flicks; winner=C1 because the pre-flick shift adds an 'anticipation' beat that strengthens the intentional, sarcastic read of the gesture.

description: The robot first makes a small 'attention' lift, then sharply moves its arm into a lateral staging position before snapping the hand to the temple and holding it rigidly.
reasoning:
# Q1: A human salute involves a sharp, direct movement of the hand from a neutral position to the forehead, often with the arm taking a specific path out to the side and then folding in.
# Q2: candidates=P1) front+horizontal+x60,y50,z40, P2) right+vertical+x55,y85,z50; winner=P1 because a neutral forward-facing start makes the subsequent formal swing out to the side and crisp fold to the temple more distinct and readable.
# Q3: options=M1 pose>pose>pose, M2 pose>path(arc), M3 pose>pose(staging)>movement(fold); winner=M3 because breaking the motion into a sharp staging move and a final crisp fold better captures the precise, angular quality of a formal salute than a single smooth arc.
# Q4: options=C1 a sharp hold at the end, C2 a slow release after the hold, C3 a preparatory 'attention' lift; winner=C1&C3 because the preparatory lift adds formality and the final hold is essential for the gesture's meaning, while a release would be a separate cue.

description: The robot raises its hand to its brow like a visor, peers forward intently, and then scans side-to-side as if searching the horizon.
reasoning:

# Q2: candidates=P1) front+horizontal+x60,y50,z70, P2) down+horizontal+x60,y50,z70; winner=P1 because the forward-pointing hand with a horizontal gripper is the most direct geometric analog to a human hand shielding the eyes to look forward.
# Q3: options=M1 pose(visor)>movement(scan), M2 pose(start)>pose(visor)>movement(peer)>movement(scan); winner=M2 because the sequence of placing the hand, peering forward, and then scanning tells a much clearer story of "searching" than a simple scan alone.
# Q4: options=C1 a forward peer before scanning, C2 a final return pose; winner=C1 because the peer strongly reinforces the intent of looking into the distance, making the subsequent scan feel motivated and specific to searching.

reasoning:

# Q2: candidates=P1) up+horizontal+x55,y60,z65, P2) front+vertical+x70,y50,z50; winner=P1 because the upward-pointing hand with an inward-facing palm is the canonical starting geometry for a finger-curling beckon.
# Q3: options=M1 pose>movement(wrist x repeat), M2 pose>pose>movement(shoulder x)>movement(wrist x repeat); winner=M2 because lifting the hand into position and extending it slightly creates a clear setup and anticipation, making the final curling motion more intentional.
# Q4: options=C1 a small forward extension before the curls, C2 a final static hold after the curls; winner=C1 because the pre-curl extension acts as an attention-getting beat that strengthens the "I'm beckoning you" context, whereas a final hold feels unnatural.

reasoning:

# Q2: candidates=P1) up+vertical+x50,y60,z40, P2) front+horizontal+x65,y50,z50; winner=P1 because the upward vertical orientation is the most natural starting pose for a celebratory upward thrust, keeping the elbow bent and ready.
# Q3: options=M1 pose>movement(down wind-up)>movement(up pump+hold), M2 pose>path(line z up only); winner=M1 because the preparatory wind-up and peak hold are essential for conveying the power and celebratory intent of the gesture, which a simple lift lacks.
# Q4: options=C1 preparatory downward wind-up before the pump, C2 a final slow return to a neutral pose; winner=C1 because the wind-up builds anticipation and makes the pump feel more explosive, whereas a slow return would kill the celebratory energy.
